newsitem.title: UK: ELF EXPECTS TO RENEW 20,000 BPD IRAQ OIL CONTRACT.
newsitem.headline: ELF EXPECTS TO RENEW 20,000 BPD IRAQ OIL CONTRACT.

text.p: French oil major Elf said on Thursday it expected to renew a 20,000 barrel a day (bpd) crude contract with Baghdad under the second phase of the U.N.'s oil-for-food exchange.
"We will probably get the same volume as before, 20,000 barrels a day, maybe slightly more but definitely not double or triple," an Elf spokesman said.
He said Elf had been invited to Baghdad next week to discuss the terms of the contract and expected to lift its first cargo toward the end of August.
Elf's contract under the first phase of the U.N. arrangement which started last December provided for 20,000 bpd of Iraqi Kirkuk crude from Iraq's Turkish pipeline outlet at Ceyhan.
Iraqi oil is due to start flowing again soon after a two-month delay during which Baghdad negotiated modifications to aid distribution plans.
The oil-for-food programme was designed to alleviate the impact on Iraqi civilians of sanctions imposed on Iraq after its troops invaded Kuwait in August 1990.
